newsitem.title: FRANCE: France sets key telecom rates ahead of competition.
newsitem.headline: France sets key telecom rates ahead of competition.

text.p: France on Wednesday fixed a set of telecommunications rates that are key for future rivals of France Telecom and remove an element of uncertainty ahead of the state-owned operators' partial privatisation.
The independent telecommunications regulator ART unveiled a list of so-called interconnection charges based on a detailed analysis of the costs at France Telecom.
Interconnection charges are the price France Telecom can charge to other operators for the transit of calls over its infrastructure of telephone lines and switches.
ART chairman Jean-Michel Hubert said that the resulting tariffs were slightly higher than those of British Telecommunications Plc but in line and often lower than the European average.
He told a news conference that the regulator had tried to set an "equitable" price structure that would promote competition while not damaging France Telecom.
Gerard Moine, director of external relations at France Telecom, said he was "satisfied" with the outcome of long talks with the ART.

"The publication of this interconnection catalogue gives France Telecom a clear regulatory framework as it prepares for the introduction of competition on January 1, 1998, and the company's initial public offering in May 1997," he said.
Bouygues Telecom, a future rival, said it was not satisfied.

"We had asked for a 30 percent cut from France Telecom's first proposals. What we have got is a 15 percent reduction. We are therefore dissatisfied," said Thierry Mileo, external relations director at Bouygues Telecom -- a venture of Bouygues, Italy's STET and Germany's Veba.
At Cegetel, the telecommunications venture of Generale des Eaux, BT and Mannesmann AG, there was no immediate reaction.

Moine told a news conference that there had been a reduction of between 10 and 15 percent in France Telecom's rates since January due to a new assessment of the value of assets related to the infrastructure.
Moine estimated that interconnection charges from rivals would initially represent a few hundred million francs rising to about a billion francs at the start of the next century.

ART published a document which detailed the costs of connection and various tariffs for different services in a range of time periods. It said that on average, the rates were 6.09 centimes (0.0609 franc) per minute for intra-subscriber exchange, 12.78 centimes for single transit (also called tandem) and 17.57 centimes for dual transit.
The first rate is mainly for local calls, the second for inter-regional calls while the third would apply to long distance national calls.
France Telecom showed that in a comparison of peak-time full-rate calls, its intra subscriber rate was slightly above that of the United Kingdom but below those in Spain, Sweden and Denmark.
Its single transit rate was higher than in the U.K. and Sweden and the double transit rate was only lower than Spain's.

France Telecom said the interconnection rates complemented its policy of tariff rebalancing for clients with planned cuts of at least nine percent per year in 1997-1998 and cuts of at least 4.5 percent per year in the period 1999-2000.
